# Helping Your Midwife Find You

**Riverside Community Midwives — a guide to getting us to your door**

Hello, and welcome to Riverside Community Midwives.

I'm one of the midwives on the team, and I've been asked to write this page because I am, without question, the one who gets lost the most. I've been doing this job a long time and I can still end up in the wrong street with the sat nav telling me I've arrived.

So please read this as me asking for a favour, not telling you off. When you're in labour and it's three in the morning, every minute matters. The quicker we get through your door, the quicker we can get on with the job. Most of what's below takes five minutes to sort out now, and saves us a lot of stress later.

---

## The short version

If you only read one bit, read this:

- **Ring the Riverside birth line when labour starts** — not our personal mobiles.
- **Two midwives come, usually in two cars.** Two parking spaces if you can.
- **Light on, number visible, path clear.**
- **Pets in another room.**
- **Don't tidy the whole house. Just clear a path.**

---

## When we can come to you

Home birth cover starts at **37 weeks**. Before 37 weeks, the plan is for you to give birth in hospital.

We tell everyone this at booking, and it's one of those things that's easy to forget once you're past 30 weeks and thinking about the pool and the playlist. If you go into labour before 37 weeks, ring the birth line and we'll talk you through what to do. From 37 weeks, we're coming to you.

---

## Two midwives, two cars

For a home birth, two midwives come. We usually drive separately, so if you can, please think about **two parking spaces**.

We also turn up with a lot of kit. The big bag, gas and air cylinders, and sometimes the birthing pool stuff. By the time we've carried it all up your path, our arms are tired and our language can get colourful. A space near the door is a real gift.

---

## Parking permits

If you live in a permit zone — especially around Anfield and Kensington — please get a visitor permit from the council, or have one ready on the dashboard.

We have been ticketed before. We would rather spend that money on biscuits.

---

## How to call us

This is the important one.

**When labour starts, ring the Riverside birth line.** Not my mobile, not any of our personal numbers. The birth line goes straight to whoever is on call, so you'll always get the midwife who can actually come to you.

**Riverside Birth Line: [insert number here]**

Save it in your phone now, before you need it. Put it under something you'll spot at 3am, like "Riverside Birth Line — CALL THIS ONE".

If you're not sure whether it's labour, ring anyway. We'd much rather have a chat than have you sitting at home worrying.

---

## Getting us to your front door

A few things that have happened to me on the way to a birth:

**The flats in Everton.** I once drove round the same block for 20 minutes because flat 14 was not next to flat 13. It was in the other building. The dad ended up waving a tea towel out of the window. Bless him. It worked, eventually.

**Rosemary Cottage.** A house with a name and no number, in a street of terraces. The sat nav took me to a chip shop. I'm not joking.

**The wrong house.** I once walked into the wrong house because the door was open. A lovely old man gave me a Jammie Dodger and pointed me next door. No harm done, but I'd rather not make a habit of it.

### What helps

- **Balloons on the gate**, like for a party. Best idea ever. I found the house straight away and it made me smile.
- **Porch light on at night.** Dark winter streets all look the same.
- **A clear number**, or the house name plus the street name. If you're set back from the road, tell us what to look for.
- **what3words**, or a **WhatsApp pin sent to the birth line phone**. Both are genuinely good, especially for flats and new builds.
- **A quick text** with the door code, which buzzer, or "we're the one with the blue door". All helpful.

---

## Pets

I love dogs. I really do. But not during the pushing stage.

Please put pets in another room before we arrive. We had a staffie called Pippin once who loved me a bit too much and jumped up every visit. I nearly dropped the Entonox. Pippin was gorgeous. Pippin was also a hazard.

---

## Inside the house

Please clear the stairs and hallway. No shoes, no washing basket, no Lego. We're carrying heavy things and we don't want to trip.

A clear path from the front door to the room you're giving birth in makes a big difference. You don't need a show home. You just need a route.

---

## How we come

In the Philippines, we say the midwife is like family. That's how we think of it too.

We're not coming to inspect your house or judge your washing pile. We're coming as a friend, to help you meet your baby. So don't tidy up for us. Just clear a path, put the light on, and put the kettle on if you like.

---

## Fridge checklist

Cut this out and stick it on the fridge. Tick as you go.

- [ ] I've saved the Riverside birth line number in my phone
- [ ] I know to ring the birth line, not my midwife's personal mobile
- [ ] I know home birth cover starts at 37 weeks
- [ ] I've thought about two parking spaces
- [ ] I have a visitor permit ready (if I live in a permit zone)
- [ ] My house number or name is easy to see from the street
- [ ] My porch light works
- [ ] I've got balloons or something to mark the gate (optional, but brilliant)
- [ ] I've sent a what3words or WhatsApp pin to the birth line
- [ ] Pets will be in another room
- [ ] Stairs and hallway are clear
- [ ] My birth partner knows where this list is

**Our door code / buzzer:** ______________________________

**Best place to park:** ______________________________

**Pets (and where they'll be):** ______________________________

**Anything else we should know:** ______________________________

---

If anything here isn't clear, ask us at your next appointment. No question is silly.

We'll see you soon. Hopefully not from the wrong side of a hedge.

*Written by one of your Riverside midwives — the one with the map upside down.*
